Fit an event rate model in one step

Source: R/event_rate.R
fit_event_rate.Rd

fit_event_rate() chains build_event_panel(), specify_event_rate(), and fit(): it computes effective exposures, attributes events to segments, and fits a Poisson rate model to the count/exposure panel with log(exposure) (in exposure_units) as the offset. The model is fitted with infer's native machinery rather than by aggregating rates externally; if the model is not estimable, the function errors.

Usage

fit_event_rate(
  online,
  events,
  exclude = NULL,
  period,
  covariates = NULL,
  formula,
  exposure_unit = NULL,
  device = "device",
  id = "event_id",
  time = "time",
  start = "start",
  end = "end",
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'event_rate_fit'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

online

A data frame of online coverage intervals with columns giving the device, the interval start, and the interval end. Intervals may overlap.

events

A data frame of events with columns giving the device, a stable event ID, and the event time. Rows sharing an event ID are treated as retries of the same event and counted once; conflicting device or time values for the same ID raise an error.

exclude

An optional data frame of exclusion intervals (e.g. maintenance periods), structured like online, to subtract from the merged online coverage.

period

A vector of length 2, c(start, end), giving the reporting period. Only coverage inside this window counts as exposure, and only events inside it are counted. Boundaries are half-open.

covariates

An optional data frame of fixed device covariates, with exactly one row per device and the same device column as the inputs to build_event_panel(). Every device with effective exposure must be present.

formula

A model formula with the panel's events column on the left-hand side and device covariates on the right-hand side, e.g. events ~ region. Use events ~ 1 for an intercept-only (overall rate) model.

exposure_unit

The unit in which exposure is expressed. For Date or POSIXct time variables, one of "seconds", "minutes", "hours", "days" (the default), or "weeks". For numeric time variables, a single positive number giving the number of native time units per exposure unit (default 1).

device, id, time, start, end

Strings naming the device column (shared by all inputs), the event ID column, the event time column, and the interval start and end columns.

...

Additional arguments passed to fit(), e.g. family.

x

For the print method, an event_rate_fit object.

Value

An object of class event_rate_fit, a list with components:

  • contributions: The interval contributions—per device and segment, the effective exposure and event count entering the model.

  • attribution: The event attribution—per unique event, the segment it was counted towards, if any.

  • ids: The IDs actually entering the model: devices (devices with effective exposure) and events (unique event IDs counted).

  • fit: The native model coefficients, as returned by fit().

  • object: The infer object produced by specify_event_rate().

See also

Other event rate functions: build_event_panel(), specify_event_rate()

Examples

online <- data.frame(
  device = c("a", "a", "b"),
  start = c(0, 5, 0),
  end = c(10, 15, 8)
)
events <- data.frame(
  device = c("a", "a", "b"),
  event_id = c("e1", "e1", "e2"),
  time = c(3, 3, 7)
)
covariates <- data.frame(
  device = c("a", "b"),
  region = c("north", "south")
)

fit_event_rate(
  online,
  events,
  period = c(0, 20),
  covariates = covariates,
  formula = events ~ region
)
#> # Event rate model fit
#> Exposure unit: native time units
#> Devices in model: 2
#> Events in model: 2
#> 
#> # A tibble: 2 × 2
#>   term        estimate
#>   <chr>          <dbl>
#> 1 intercept     -2.71 
#> 2 regionsouth    0.629
